job.title: Add fluent batch response-header removal to Fastify
job.goal: Add reply.removeHeaders(names), a fluent API that takes an array of header-name strings, removes those response headers case-insensitively using the same behavior as reply.removeHeader, and returns the same reply instance. An empty array is a no-op. Duplicate and missing names are harmless. Validate the entire input before mutation: non-array inputs or any non-string element must throw TypeError and leave all headers unchanged. Update the public TypeScript Reply interface and document the new API. Preserve existing behavior and all original tests and CI files; new test files are allowed. Discover and run the repository's substantive existing test suite, including relevant type checks when executable, and verify behavior through real Fastify requests. No production deployment is requested.

plan.setup:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
cd /workspace

node -v
npm -v

# Install all dependencies from project metadata (no package-lock ships; .npmrc sets package-lock=false).
npm install --ignore-scripts

# Guard against the ERR_REQUIRE_ESM regression: the latest light-my-request@6.x (6.2.0+)
# declares cookie ^1.0.1 or ^2.0.0; cookie@2.x is { "type":"module" } ESM-only,
# so require('cookie') inside light-my-request/lib/request.js fails with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM.
# Pin light-my-request to 6.0.0 (declares cookie ^0.6.0, the CJS require()-able line)
# via --no-save so package.json is left untouched.
npm install light-my-request@6.0.0 --no-save --ignore-scripts

# Verify the cookie CJS entry that light-my-request requires actually loads.
if [ ! -f node_modules/cookie/index.js ]; then
  echo "cookie CJS entry (index.js) missing; require('cookie') would fail. Aborting."
  exit 1
fi
if [ -f node_modules/cookie/package.json ]; then
  cookie_type=$(node -e "try{console.log(require('node:fs').readFileSync('node_modules/cookie/package.json','utf8').match(/\"type\"\s*:\s*\"module\"/)?'module':'cjs')}catch(e){console.log('cjs')}")
  if [ "$cookie_type" = "module" ]; then
    echo "cookie is ESM (type:module); require('cookie') would fail. Aborting."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

node -e "require('cookie'); console.log('require cookie OK')" || { echo "require(\"cookie\") failed in setup"; exit 1; }

echo "setup complete"

plan.rationale: Prior execution feedback: setup succeeded (code 0) and all three preservation checks passed (preserve-reply-suite code 0, preserve-typescript-import code 0, preserve-typescript-reply-tsd code 0). The behavior requirement check failed on original source as intended (code 1, accepted true): subtests 1, 3, 6 fail with 'removeHeaders is not a function' / header-still-present assertions. The negative-control mutation (removeHeader returns null) was correctly detected (preserve-reply-suite failed, 2 failures). The typed check (require-removeheaders-typed) failed on original source as intended (code 1, accepted true) with a captured, controlled TS2551 'Property removeHeaders does not exist' diagnostic. All checks are accepted. The ONLY rejection from the prior round was a single blocking review finding: the explicit customer requirement to 'document the new API' (docs/Reference/Reply.md, deliverables[2]) had no verification check, so an executor could omit the docs and still pass. FIX (the only change): add require-removeheaders-docs, which greps docs/Reference/Reply.md for the TOC entry '[.removeHeaders(names)](#removeheadersnames)', the summary bullet backticked '.removeHeaders(names)', the '### .removeHeaders(names)' section heading, and the '' anchor. On original source all are absent, so the check fails (missing-feature); on the documented implementation all are present and it passes. Every other script is unchanged from the prior accepted plan. Goal: add reply.removeHeaders(names) to Fastify's Reply prototype. Implementation (lib/reply.js, inserted immediately after the existing removeHeader at lines 237-241): removeHeader does `delete this[kReplyHeaders][key.toLowerCase()]; return this`. removeHeaders(names) will: (1) validate Array.isArray(names), else throw TypeError; (2) iterate every element and throw TypeError on the first where typeof !== 'string' BEFORE any mutation (validate-before-mutate), so all headers stay unchanged on invalid input; (3) for each name perform the same lowercasing-delete via this.removeHeader(name) — case-insensitive, duplicate/missing harmless; (4) return this (same reply instance). An empty array short-circuits to return this (no-op). This reuses the exact lowercasing-delete of removeHeader so existing semantics are preserved. TypeScript (types/reply.d.ts): add a sibling declaration after the removeHeader line (line 58): `removeHeaders(names: HttpHeader[]): FastifyReply;` mirroring removeHeader's return type and using the same HttpHeader element type as removeHeader's key parameter. Docs (docs/Reference/Reply.md): add a TOC entry ` - [.removeHeaders(names)](#removeheadersnames)` after the `.removeHeader(key)` line (line 14), a summary bullet `- \`.removeHeaders(names)\` - Remove the values of previously set headers.` after line 59, and a new `### .removeHeaders(names)` section with `` after the `.removeHeader(key)` section (which ends at line 227, before `.hasHeader`). Preservation: removeHeader is untouched; the new method delegates to the same lowercasing-delete. The preserve-reply-suite check runs test/internals/reply.test.js, which at line 1268 asserts reply.removeHeader('x-foo') === reply strictly, so the negative-control mutation changing `return this` to `return null` inside removeHeader makes that preservation check fail with an assertion error. Requirement checks verify the real requested behavior via app.inject (the real Fastify request lifecycle): batch removal, case-insensitivity, returns-the-same-instance, empty-array no-op, duplicate/missing harmlessness, TypeError on non-array (string/object/number/null), TypeError on any non-string element, validate-before-mutate (headers unchanged when a later element is invalid), and fluent chaining with removeHeader. On original source the behavior test throws `reply.removeHeaders is not a function` (a clear missing-feature TypeError); the typed check fails with a captured TS2551; the docs check fails with a missing TOC entry. All three pass on the correct implementation.
limitations: The full borp suite (184 test files) is not run in every check because many spawn live HTTP servers with timeouts (70 test files use fastify.listen + simple-get) and the http2 tests require h2url; running all would exceed per-check limits and several reference external hostnames in their request fixtures (e.g. constrained-routes.test.js uses 'example.com'/'google.com' as constrained-route Host values, which is fine offline, but the http2 h2url tests need an h2 client). test/internals/reply.test.js (asserting at line 1268 that removeHeader returns the reply instance, so the negative-control mutation makes it fail) is run as a preservation check covering the header/removeHeader surface; the tsc import check and a tsd run scoped to test/types/reply.test-d.ts cover the TypeScript surface.

The default tsd run (tsd.directory = test/types) includes register.test-d.ts, which has a pre-existing failure: the installed pino's BaseLogger requires msgPrefix that the test's custom logger type lacks (a version-drift issue from package-lock=false, unrelated to this change). The preserve-typescript-reply-tsd check scopes tsd to test/types/reply.test-d.ts via --files to avoid that pre-existing failure; the full tsd is deliberately not run as a gate because it fails on original source independent of this change.

No package-lock ships with the repo (.npmrc sets package-lock=false), so dependency versions resolve from the registry at install time. To keep the suite reproducible and avoid the ERR_REQUIRE_ESM regression seen when the latest light-my-request 6.x hoists cookie@2.x (ESM-only, type:module), setup pins light-my-request to 6.0.0 (whose cookie dep is the CJS 0.6.x line, require()-able) via --no-save so package.json is left untouched.
No production deployment is requested; behavior is verified through app.inject (the real Fastify request lifecycle via light-my-request) rather than a live network server.

tsd reads its test directory from package.json (test/types), which is a protected path and therefore read-only at check time, so the typed requirement check uses tsc --noEmit on a temp file in /workspace instead of writing a new .test-d.ts into test/types.

protected_paths intentionally covers only test/ and .github/ (original tests and CI). The deliverables lib/reply.js, types/reply.d.ts and docs/Reference/Reply.md must be modified to deliver the feature and therefore are NOT protected; source/documentation that must change cannot be immutable.

The documentation requirement check (require-removeheaders-docs) inspects docs/Reference/Reply.md (a deliverable, not protected) for the TOC entry, summary bullet, section heading, and anchor. It fails on original source where these are absent.
